what: NOT the T3.2 gate. A shape/indexing smoke of the comparison core plus a measurement of how much of T3.2's budget the fp16 storage of logits.bin spends before PyTorch is involved.
method: compare_shard() fed log(logits.bin) as a stand-in for the HF side. Monotone, so the ranks are identical by construction and the comparison should be perfect.
finding: It is not 1.0. topk.bin records llama.cpp's argsort over fp32 selection_probs; logits.bin stores those probabilities in fp16, and at a near-tie the rounding reorders them. Storage alone therefore consumes ~1 point of the 3 available under the 0.97 exact_match floor and about half of the 0.001 available under the 0.999 set_agreement floor.
caveat: An upper bound, not a prediction: the real HF side arrives in fp32, closer to llama.cpp's fp32 probabilities than the fp16 round trip. Recorded so a marginal T3.2 result is checked against this before anyone hunts a harness bug.
spearman_note: 1.000000 on every layer confirms the I13 substitution is sound -- logits.bin is post-softmax, and softmax preserves ranks, so the plan's 'Spearman on raw logits' gate survives it.
still_required: The real T3.2 run on Kaggle against allenai/OLMoE-1B-7B-0125 in fp16. This file establishes nothing about llama.cpp's correctness.
